description: A login form with real rate-limit UX: a visible lockout countdown after failed attempts.

files.content:
# Login Guard

A login form that just returns "incorrect password" forever, with no rate limiting, is an open invitation to brute-force. But most tutorial login forms skip that part entirely — they show the happy path and stop there.

## The solution

A login form with real rate-limit UX: after 3 failed attempts, the form locks out with a visible countdown before you can try again. It's demo credentials only (`demo@example.com` / `correct-horse`), all client-side — the point is the UX pattern and the Playwright suite that verifies it, not a real auth backend.

## How to use it

Open `index.html` in a browser and try the demo credentials, or try wrong ones a few times to see the lockout.

## Running the tests

```
npm install
npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
npm test
```

One test in `tests/login.spec.js` is **deliberately failing** — it's a contributor exercise (see the comment above it in the file for the reasoning).

## How it's built

Plain JavaScript, no framework. Failed attempts are tracked in memory; on the third failure a countdown `setInterval` disables the submit button and updates the status message every second until it expires. The Playwright suite drives the real page via `page.goto("file://...")` — no dev server needed.

## Contribute

- Fix the deliberately failing test in `tests/login.spec.js` (or fix the code, if you decide the test's expectation was actually correct).
- Add a test for the case where a user starts typing again after being locked out — right now the form doesn't clear the fields or give feedback until the button re-enables.
- Persist `failedAttempts` to `sessionStorage` so a page refresh doesn't reset the lockout — currently reloading the page resets attempts to zero, defeating the whole point.

Scaffolded by an automated weekly pipeline, then refined by hand — see the factory repo for how it works.

issue.title: Deliberately failing test in tests/login.spec.js needs a real fix
issue.body: The last test in `tests/login.spec.js` ("lockout message shows 25 seconds remaining immediately") fails on purpose — read the comment directly above it for why. Decide whether the *app's* copy should change (e.g. show the full LOCKOUT_SECONDS value immediately and start counting down from there differently) or whether the *test's* expectation is simply wrong, then fix whichever one is actually broken. Explain your reasoning in the PR description. Under an hour, and a nice exercise in reading a test's intent rather than just making it green.
